summary: jwt-logger@2.4.9 drops and executes obfuscated stage-2 payload on require()
details: The package's main module jwt-logger.js is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io rotated string-array with control-flow flattening) and executes unconditionally when the module is required. On load it creates a cache directory under the user's home, writes a second obfuscated JavaScript payload plus a synthetic package.json declaring runtime dependencies axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, socket.io-client, and koffi (on Windows), then spawns process.execPath (node) — or wscript.exe with a generated main.vbs on Windows — detached with cwd set to that directory to execute the stage-2 code. The dependency set bundled with the stage-2 runtime is the canonical remote-controlled stealer stack: better-sqlite3 for reading browser SQLite stores (cookies, saved logins), node-machine-id for host fingerprinting, koffi for native FFI (commonly used for DPAPI-based browser secret decryption on Windows), and socket.io-client for a persistent command-and-control channel back to a party operated by the author. The package advertises author 'Blake Embrey' and carries innocuous jwtLog/createLog docstrings copied from an unrelated legitimate library, but the actual module.exports has no relation to JWT logging; package.json also self-references 'jwt-logger':'^2.4.9'. The obfuscation exists solely to conceal the dropper and remote-execution chain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
